Admittedly, a Police Station has been constructed on the part of  land which belongs to the petitioner.
The area is five decimals over which the construction is made.
Admittedly, the petitioner is the title holder of the entire land including the portion over which the Police Station has been constructed, which has also been declared by a competent Civil Court.

Therefore, now the only issue which remains to be decided is whether the respondents be directed to demolish the Police Station and hand over vacant possession of the land to the petitioner or to pay compensation as per the provision of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for the five decimals of land, over which the Police Station is constructed.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: So far as vacant portion is concerned, which has been bounded by the boundary wall by the respondents will be demarcated from the five decimals of land, over which the Police Station has been constructed.
The respondents are injuncted from entering into the vacant portion i.e. the area beyond the constructed Police Station.

Whether the respondents are ready to pay compensation or they are ready to demolish the Police Station, will be informed to this Court on the next date.
List this case after two weeks.
